rounds.text: Kody Technolab Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 yielding a BUY recommendation with medium confidence [E53]. The business has delivered outstanding long-term growth, with a compounded sales growth rate of 102% over 5 years [E8] and an astonishing compounded profit growth of 189% over the same period [E11]. This impressive expansion is underpinned by a robust return on capital employed of 20.7% [E6] and a 3-year median return on equity of 20% [E15], both comfortably outperforming the sector median ROCE of 12.2% [E66]. Furthermore, the company exhibits pristine financial health by actively reducing its borrowings to Rs 8 Cr in March 2026 [E27], qualifying it as almost debt free [E48]. Operational efficiency is further signaled by capital expenditure completion, as capital work-in-progress stands at Rs 0 Cr, indicating that new capacity is ready to come online [E28]. Market validation matches these fundamental strengths, evidenced by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E39] and a positive institutional money flow [E32], all backed by a supportive Information Technology sector tailwind [E61]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E ratio of 88 [E1], a price-to-book multiple of 9.34x [E2], and a negative free cash flow of Rs -29 Cr in March 2026 [E23].

The valuation currently priced into Kody Technolab Ltd is disconnected from fundamental reality, with the stock trading at an aggressive P/E of 88 and a price-to-book multiple of 9.34x [E1, E2]. This expensive entry point leaves a staggering margin of safety of -114.6%, as a discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at just Rs 627 per share against a market price of Rs 1,345 [E33, E34]. Furthermore, today's price requires an unsustainable 28.7% earnings growth rate to justify itself, vastly outstripping the 18.0% baseline assumption [E35]. Operational quality severely undermines these lofty market expectations, highlighted by an atrocious cash conversion ratio of 0.18x where profits vastly outpace actual operating cash flow, alongside deeply negative free cash flow of Rs -29 Cr and high debtors stretching to 173 days [E21, E23, E52]. Compounding these risks, long-term operating margins have degraded from 40% down to 33%, while price growth has run 44% ahead of underlying profit growth, signaling that expectations have dangerously detached from delivery [E17, E45]. Conceded: the company demonstrates strong historical growth metrics, including a 5-year compounded sales growth of 102% and a rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 [E8, E53].

Conceded: operating cash flow against reported profit is 0.18x with negative free cash flow of Rs -29 Cr, and debtors stand at 173 days [E21, E23, E52]. However, the market's willingness to pay up for this asset is completely justified by elite fundamental momentum, including a stellar 5-year compounded sales growth of 102% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 189% [E8, E11]. This hyper-growth is backed by an exceptional rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 with a medium confidence BUY rating [E53], while institutional money flow shows positive accumulation with a holding change of +0.08 percentage points [E32]. Furthermore, the company operates with a pristine balance sheet featuring a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.04x and borrowings reduced to Rs 8 Cr [E25, E27], sitting comfortably inside an Information Technology sector experiencing robust tailwinds with a score of +0.65 [E63].

Conceded: the company demonstrates stellar 5-year compounded sales growth of 102% and a 5-year compounded profit growth of 189% [E8, E11], alongside a rules-based screen score of 86 out of 100 [E53]. However, the bull's claim that elite fundamental momentum completely justifies an aggressive P/E of 88 and a price-to-book multiple of 9.34x [E1, E2] ignores glaring cash flow divergence, evidenced by a cash conversion ratio of just 0.18x, negative free cash flow of Rs -29 Cr, and exceptionally high debtors of 173 days [E21, E23, E52]. Conceded: institutional money flow shows positive accumulation with a holding change of +0.08 percentage points and the sector experiences robust tailwinds with a score of +0.65 [E32, E63]. Yet, this institutional interest and a pristine balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.04x [E25] cannot mask the reality that today's price sits 100% of the way up its 52-week range [E5] and already discounts a demanding 28.7% earnings growth [E35], while earnings growth is actively decelerating [E58] and price growth outpaces profit delivery by 44% [E45].
